subject: Prep: Locust preflight & SLO recon — action items
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@asterbiotech.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Prep: Locust preflight & SLO recon — action items

Hi Carlos — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned before the test window: 

Summary of what we heard you need:
- SLO targets: p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 600ms for 512-token requests (text gen).
- Throughput/concurrency: target sustained ~30 QPS with spikes to 120 QPS; concurrent streaming clients ~500.
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming required for the UX; tests should exercise both streaming and non-streaming routes.

Our asks / proposed actions:
1) Confirm test window: we propose May 9, 2027 10:00–12:00 PT. Please confirm if that works or send alternatives.
2) Provide IP ranges to allowlist for the test agents / CI runners (we typically need public CIDRs for k6/Locust runners).
3) Share a small set of test accounts (or let us create scoped service accounts) with example prompts and expected output size.
4) Confirm whether the test should include long-context runs (>=2048 tokens) or capped at 512.

I've attached a small bundle with our Locust/k6 examples and a short preflight checklist (redwood-locust-examples.tar.gz). After you confirm the window and allowlist we will:
- Provision a short-lived test API key and a service account for the run.
- Provide a Locust script tuned for streaming (we have a streaming adapter prototype we can send).
- Coordinate an infra engineer (marcus) and our SRE (stephanie) to be on the call during the window.

Immediate next steps (simple):
- Carlos: confirm window OR propose alternate 2-hour slot this week. Also drop the allowlist CIDRs and test account list (a CSV will do).
- Redwood: we will prepare the streaming Locust adapter and an infra ticket to allowlist your ranges.

Thanks — I’ll follow up internally and loop in stephanie/marcus for the infra prep.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-locust-examples.tar.gz (tar.gz, 3 files: locustfile.py, README.md, streaming_adapter.py)

From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@asterbiotech.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: security@asterbiotech.com
Date: 2027-05-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prep: Locust preflight & SLO recon — action items

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. May 9 10:00–12:00 PT works for the team. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Streaming: yes, token-by-token streaming is required for our UI; we need the test to exercise real streaming sessions, not just chunked responses.
- Concurrency: 500 concurrent streaming sessions is a realistic upper bound for the test; sustained QPS target is 25–35, spike up to ~120 QPS for 30s bursts.
- Latency expectations: we will validate p95 and p99 for 512-token payloads; target p95 <= 350ms looks reasonable, p99 <= 600ms is our internal bar.
- Long contexts: for the first run, stick to 512 tokens; we can schedule a separate long-context run later.

Allowlist CIDRs for our runners (these are the external CI runners we will use):
- 52.12.64.0/24
- 3.212.11.0/24
- 34.220.0.0/20

Attached is a small CSV with the test accounts we’ll use (austin-test-accounts.csv). Security alias for allowlist coordination: security@asterbiotech.com.

Also, will you be simulating network jitter or will we run from our public runners only? We prefer to run from our runners but can add a small synthetic jitter layer if you want to validate tail latencies.

Carlos Vega
Senior Product Manager, Integrations
AsterBiotech
carlos.vega@asterbiotech.com

Attachment: austin-test-accounts.csv (CSV, 6 rows: account_id,api_key_scope,expected_avg_prompt_tokens)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@asterbiotech.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Prep: Locust preflight & SLO recon — action items

Folks — forwarding Carlos’ reply. Please see the allowlist CIDRs and test accounts attached by the customer. Action items for infra/SRE: 

- Marcus: create a short-lived service account + API key scoped to test-only ingestion (expiry: 48h). Put credentials in a secure share and DM Carlos the creation method.
- Stephanie: review the Locust examples and confirm streaming approach. If we need a websocket adapter, attach it and I’ll send it to Carlos. Also confirm whether we should ask the customer to run from their runners or if we spin up our own agents (they prefer their runners).
- Both: open an allowlist ticket with networking for the CIDRs and mark the ticket P2 (test window May 9).

Carlos — we will reply with the test API key workflow and the Locust streaming adapter by EOD tomorrow (May 3). If you want us to run agents from our side as well for a cross-compare, tell us and we’ll schedule additional capacity.

Onward,
Vanessa

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-02T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Prep: Locust preflight & SLO recon — action items

Thanks — we got it. Short update: 

- Marcus will open the allowlist ticket with networking and include the three CIDRs; expect a confirmation by EOD May 4.
- I’ll prepare a Locust streaming adapter (we’ll rely on the customer runners but provide a small agent pool from our side for cross-compare). Attaching the adapter prototype (locust-streaming-adapter.py).
- I will also create a scoped, expiring API key and post the secure link here once ready; plan is to have keys + adapter by EOD May 3 for you to validate.

If Carlos wants synthetic jitter, we can add a thin proxy that adds configurable 10–50ms jitter to mimic mobile networks — let us know and we’ll include a test flag.

-steph
Stephanie Nguyen
SRE (Platform Reliability)
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
